cvEn:
Dan (Danny) Erel Angel, son of Pesah and Sara, was born on the first day of Adar 5705 (14 February 1945) in Tel Aviv. He completed his studies at the Yehuda HaLevi elementary school in Tel Aviv. He then attended the Real School in Haifa, where he lived in its military boarding school. He was drafted into the IDF in August 1962 and served in the Air Force as a pilot. After completing his compulsory service, he joined the regular army. He served as a Lieutenant and was admired by all his comrades in the service. He was a pilot in the Air Force's aerobatic formation and was considered an excellent instructor.

On the first day of fighting in the Six-Day War, the 26th of Iyar 5727 (5 June 1967), Dan fell in an air battle. He fell over Egyptian skies during the attack on the Inshas airfield, and his burial place is unknown. A memorial headstone was set up in the plot for the missing in the Mount Herzl cemetery in Jerusalem. After his death he was promoted to the rank of Captain. A grove of a thousand trees was planted in his memory in the Modi'in Forest near Ben Shemen; the grove is adjacent to the one bearing the name of Eli Cohen. In the Antopol Martyrs Synagogue in Tel Aviv, his father set up an Ark of the Torah with an eternal light in his memory, and a marble plaque was placed there as well. A corner with a library in his name was established in the elementary school where he studied. He is listed as an MIA (missing in action), a soldier whose burial place is unknown.
